concerns.text: T014a mandates raising RuntimeError if CUDA is available. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires results to be reproducible on a fresh runner; the code must enforce CPU execution via device assignment without failing the run if GPU hardware is present, as the environment dictates the runner type, not the code crashing.

Tasks T008b/c/e implement a fallback logic (LMM -> Stratified -> Normality Check -> t-test/Wilcoxon) that contradicts spec.md FR-005. FR-005 mandates LMM (or Stratified if infeasible) as the primary comparison, with Normality checks determining the *post-hoc* test type for the *final* comparison. The task logic conflates the model selection with the post-hoc test selection, risking incorrect statistical application (e.g., applying Wilcoxon to LMM residuals instead of raw score differences).

T029a defines 'Forgetting Violation' as 'any deviation from deletion compliance' but the sampling logic relies on a 'total failure count N'. The spec (FR-007) requires sampling failure cases (False Positives + False Negatives + Forgetting Violations). The task description is circular and lacks a precise definition of what constitutes a 'Forgetting Violation' episode in the context of the sampling logic (i.e., is it a case where deletion was requested but data remained?), creating ambiguity that prevents strict adherence to the spec's sampling criteria.

T018 (Access Control) and T023 (Utility) are split by User Story/Domain. Spec.md FR-004 requires calculating *all three* core metrics (Utility, Access Control, Forgetting) for *every* test episode to enable the paired comparison required by FR-005. Splitting metric calculation by domain/user story implies Access Control is only calculated for US1 and Utility only for US2, violating the requirement for a unified dataset analysis.

T014a specifies loading a 'frozen DistilBERT intent classifier' with a default of 'distilbert-base-uncased'. Spec.md FR-002 requires a 'CPU-tractable gatekeeper pipeline' with an 'intent classifier'. A raw base model has no intent classification head trained on the specific 'leak-target' schema, rendering it functionally useless for the benchmark. The task must specify a zero-shot classifier (e.g., BART-MNLI as per plan.md) or a training step, otherwise the deliverable fails to satisfy the functional requirement of an 'intent classifier'.

T006d requires runtime checksum verification against 'state/artifact_hashes.yaml' which is populated by T006a. In a clean environment (Constitution Principle I), T006d will fail immediately on the first run because the checksum file does not exist yet. The task logic creates a 'chicken-and-egg' failure condition that violates the requirement for a reproducible, automated run on a fresh runner unless the validation logic explicitly handles the 'missing file' case as a 'first run' trigger.
